CTMT_definition.statement: A residual closure attempt on a typed carrier C exhibits CTMT when available operational identities and structural reductions reduce the closure question to a carrier-native matrix-element family M(alpha,beta,gamma)=<a_alpha,P_beta b_gamma>, with carrier-native vectors/projections/transports, while inherited records neither supply enough kernel/transport data to compute M nor make the M-decision target-equivalent.

CTMT_consequence_theorem.statement: When a typed carrier exhibits CTMT, the framework output is the exact carrier-native M-family and one of three typed outcomes: CTMT-stuck, CTMT-foreclosed-numerical, or CTMT-bridge-failure.
CTMT_consequence_theorem.CTMT_stuck: The M-family is the precise external-content interface; external work supplying the missing kernel/transport data resolves the route.
CTMT_consequence_theorem.CTMT_foreclosed_numerical: A lawful alternate chain computes an M-value nonzero with sharp lower bound; the route is foreclosed under inherited normalization.
CTMT_consequence_theorem.CTMT_bridge_failure: The M-family is not defined across the carriers; the carrier-pivot fails under inherited records.
